local ACCEL_MIN_DUR = 400000000
local inEvent = false
local eventStart = 0
local eventPeak = 0

for i = 0, accel:size() - 1 do
  local s = accel:at(i)
  local a = s.v
  if math.abs(a) > ACCEL_THRESH then
    if not inEvent then
      inEvent = true
      eventStart = s.t
      eventPeak = a
    elseif math.abs(a) > math.abs(eventPeak) then
      eventPeak = a
    end
  elseif inEvent then

    if dur >= ACCEL_MIN_DUR then

      closeMarker(s.t, {label = string.format("%s (peak %.1f m/s^2)", label, eventPeak)})

Analysis complete. Here's what I built and what it reveals.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`create_derived_series` joins multi-input transforms on **exact timestamp equality** — that's why `lateral_accel_expected` (yaw_rate × speed) failed: the IMU runs on its own 99.1 Hz clock and `vehicle_speed` on a separate 30.0 Hz CAN-derived clock, so they never share a timestamp. This is a deliberate constraint, not a bug — silently interpolating across two independent clocks would let you fabricate correlations. For a real interpolated join you'd need the marker engine's `atTime()`, which is only available in the marker-rule sandbox, not in derived series.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Derived series created (Custom Series panel)
- **`speed_from_gps`** — finite-difference of `current_pose/pose/position` (x,y), an independent check on `vehicle_speed`.
- **`accel_horizontal_mag`** — √(ax²+ay²) from the IMU, a comfort/aggressiveness metric independent of gravity bias.
- **`mag_field_magnitude`** — √(x²+y²+z²) of the magnetometer, to sanity-check the sensor against Earth's field.

## Markers (9 global regions, visible on every plot)
One combined rule scanning the IMU and speed channels for three sustained conditions: harsh longitudinal accel/braking (|ax|>4 m/s² for ≥0.4s), cornering/maneuvering (|yaw rate|>0.25 rad/s for ≥0.5s), and stopped (speed<0.3 m/s for ≥1s).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
I deliberately required each condition to *persist* rather than firing on any single sample over threshold. IMU noise routinely produces single-sample excursions several sigma from the mean — at 99 Hz that's normal vibration, not an event. Requiring the condition to hold for hundreds of milliseconds is what keeps this at 9 clean regions instead of a wall of thousands of one-sample lines.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What the data shows

**Single acceleration run, not stop-and-go traffic.** ~231.5 s total: low-speed maneuvering with a large heading change from t≈0–90s, a smooth ramp to a ~19–21 m/s cruise (≈70–75 km/h) held from t≈150–200s, then deceleration back to a stop by t≈230s. Position traces a near-straight line in the local frame (x: 0→‑1519 m, y: 0→+1786 m) — consistent heading (~2.0–2.35 rad) throughout the cruise, bracketed by real turning maneuvers at the start and end (these are exactly the "cornering" marker regions).

**A standout anomaly around t≈185s.** Longitudinal acceleration spikes from -12.1 to +9.2 m/s² in well under half a second — far larger than any other excursion in the whole run (typical peaks elsewhere are ±5–9 m/s² during the acceleration ramp). `accel_horizontal_mag` peaks at 12.1 there too. This is a genuine outlier, worth checking against video/lidar if you have it — most likely a pothole/speed bump, but a sensor glitch can't be ruled out from IMU data alone. I'd treat this as the single highest-priority thing to review.

**GPS-derived speed is noisy, use with caution.** `speed_from_gps` roughly tracks `vehicle_speed`'s shape but has spikes up to 525 m/s and a much higher mean (22 vs 11.5 m/s) — a symptom of non-uniform ~20 Hz sample timing (small Δt in the denominator amplifies any position jitter). It's useful as a rough independent cross-check, not a clean speed signal.

**Magnetometer looks healthy.** Magnitude sits at ~48.7 µT with only ~9% variation — right in Earth's normal field range, no sign of magnetic interference from the vehicle during the drive.

**Roll/pitch stay small** (under ~0.1 rad / 5.7°) the whole trip — flat road, no rollover or extreme pitch events, so it's safe to treat this as ground-vehicle-normal dynamics.

**One thing I couldn't check automatically:** `/nissan/gps/duro/status_string` is textual (GPS fix status), and my tools can only read numeric series — I'd suggest you eyeball that string around the low-speed startup phase and the t≈185s anomaly, in case it correlates with a fix-mode change rather than a road event.
